##### Homogeneous network interference

The assumption of [*homogeneous network interference*](#def-homogeneous-network-interference) holds that each exposure mapping is [separable](#def-separability), and that its [component functions](#def-separability) are [positionally invariant](#def-positional-invariance) and [bounded](#def-boundedness). Positional invariance says that a unit's network value depends on its neighbors' values only through the pairs of each neighbor's value and weight, through one function that is the same for every unit, whatever its position in the network: neighbors with equal weights are interchangeable. Boundedness says that network values lie in a finite set.
